title: Self-Supervised Laplace Approximation for Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification
summary: Approximate Bayesian inference typically revolves around computing the posterior parameter distribution. In practice, however, the main object of interest is often a model's predictions rather than its parameters. In this work, we propose to bypass the parameter posterior and focus directly on approximating the posterior predictive distribution. We achieve this by drawing inspiration from self-training within self-supervised and semi-supervised learning. Essentially, we quantify a Bayesian model's predictive uncertainty by refitting on self-predicted data. The idea is strikingly simple: If a model assigns high likelihood to self-predicted data, these predictions are of low uncertainty, and vice versa. This yields a deterministic, sampling-free approximation of the posterior predictive. The modular structure of our Self-Supervised Laplace Approximation (SSLA) further allows us to plug in different prior specifications, enabling classical Bayesian sensitivity (w.r.t. prior choice) analysis. In order to bypass expensive refitting, we further introduce an approximate version of SSLA, called ASSLA. We study (A)SSLA both theoretically and empirically in regression models ranging from Bayesian linear models to Bayesian neural networks. Across a wide array of regression tasks with simulated and real-world datasets, our methods outperform classical Laplace approximations in predictive calibration while remaining computationally efficient.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Self-Supervised Laplace Approximation (SSLA) and its approximate version (ASSLA) for Bayesian uncertainty quantification. Instead of directly approximating the posterior parameter distribution, it focuses on approximating the posterior predictive distribution by refitting the model on self-predicted data. The likelihood of self-predicted data is used as an indicator of prediction uncertainty. The implementation uses Bayesian linear models and Bayesian Neural Networks for regression tasks.
data_sources: The paper uses both simulated and real-world datasets for regression tasks. The specific nature of the real-world datasets is not revealed, but if the core methodology works well with financial time series data, it will become relevant in quantitative trading.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in better quantifying uncertainty in model predictions. In trading, accurate uncertainty estimation can be crucial for risk management, position sizing, and deciding when to abstain from trading. If SSLA/ASSLA provides more reliable uncertainty estimates than traditional methods (like standard Laplace approximation) when applied to forecasting asset returns, volatility, or other key financial variables, it could lead to improved risk-adjusted returns.

title: On the Importance of Multistability for Horizon Generalization in Reinforcement Learning
summary: In reinforcement learning (RL), agents acting in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) must rely on memory, typically encoded in a recurrent neural network (RNN), to integrate information from past observations. Long-horizon POMDPs, in which the relevant observation and the optimal action are separated by many time steps (called the horizon), are particularly challenging: training suffers from poor generalization, severe sample inefficiency, and prohibitive exploration costs. Ideally, an agent trained on short horizons would retain optimal behavior at arbitrarily longer ones, but no formal framework currently characterizes when this is achievable. To fill this gap, we formalized temporal horizon generalization, the property that a policy remains optimal for all horizons, derived a necessary and sufficient condition for it, and experimentally evaluated the ability of nonlinear and parallelizable RNN variants to achieve it. This paper presents the resulting theoretical framework, the empirical evaluation, and the dynamical interpretation linking RNN behavior to temporal horizon generalization. Our analyses reveal that multistability is necessary for temporal horizon generalization and, in simple tasks, sufficient; more complex tasks further require transient dynamics. In contrast, modern parallelizable architectures, namely state space models and gated linear RNNs, are monostable by construction and consequently fail to generalize across temporal horizons. We conclude that multistability and transient dynamics are two essential and complementary dynamical regimes for horizon generalization, and that no current parallelizable RNN exhibits both. Designing parallelizable architectures that combine these regimes thus emerges as a key direction for scalable long-horizon RL.
core_methodology: The paper develops a theoretical framework for temporal horizon generalization in reinforcement learning (RL), specifically focusing on partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). It investigates the role of multistability and transient dynamics in recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for enabling RL agents to maintain optimal behavior across varying time horizons. The paper derives a necessary and sufficient condition for horizon generalization and experimentally evaluates different RNN architectures, including nonlinear, parallelizable, and gated linear RNNs, to assess their ability to achieve it. The analysis centers around identifying dynamical regimes that support horizon generalization.
data_sources: The paper uses simulated POMDP environments for experimental evaluation, rather than real-world financial data.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in developing more robust and stable RL agents for long-horizon trading strategies. If an agent can be trained on shorter timeframes and generalize to longer horizons reliably, it could reduce training costs and improve performance in complex market scenarios requiring memory of past events and anticipation of future outcomes. Multistability in RNNs could potentially lead to a better capture of regime changes and persistence in financial markets. Successful application would require translating the theoretical findings to architectures capable of processing financial time series effectively and identifying suitable POMDP formulations of common trading problems.

title: Investigating simple target-covariate relationships for Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS
summary: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) have recently achieved state-of-the-art performance, often outperforming supervised models in zero-shot settings. Recent TSFM architectures, such as Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS, aim to integrate covariates. In this paper, we design controlled experiments based on simple target-covariate relationships to assess this integration capability. Our results show that TabPFN-TS captures these relationships more effectively than Chronos-2, especially for short horizons, suggesting that the strong benchmark performance of Chronos-2 does not automatically translate into optimal modeling of simple covariate-target dependencies.

data_sources: The paper uses synthetic data designed for controlled experiments to evaluate the target-covariate relationships. It doesn't specify the usage of real-world market data.
alpha_potential: While the paper doesn't directly provide a trading strategy, understanding how TSFMs handle covariates is crucial for incorporating exogenous variables (e.g., macroeconomic indicators, sentiment data) into forecasting models. If TabPFN-TS truly outperforms Chronos-2 in capturing covariate relationships, it could lead to improved predictions and construction of trading signals based on external market drivers. This is especially relevant for short-term trading strategies.

title: Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Sequential Decision Making
summary: Information-theoretic generalization bounds based on the supersample construction are a central tool for algorithm-dependent generalization analysis in the batch i.i.d.~setting. However, existing supersample conditional mutual information (CMI) bounds do not directly apply to sequential decision-making problems such as online learning, streaming active learning, and bandits, where data are revealed adaptively and the learner evolves along a causal trajectory. To address this limitation, we develop a sequential supersample framework that separates the learner filtration from a proof-side enlargement used for ghost-coordinate comparisons. Under a row-wise exchangeability assumption, the sequential generalization gap is controlled by sequential CMI, a sum of roundwise selector--loss information terms. We also establish a Bernstein-type refinement that yields faster rates under suitable variance conditions. The selector-SCMI proof strategy applies to online learning, streaming active learning with importance weighting, and stochastic multi-armed bandits.
core_methodology: The paper develops a sequential supersample framework and uses sequential conditional mutual information (SCMI) to derive generalization bounds for sequential decision-making problems. It leverages row-wise exchangeability assumptions and provides a Bernstein-type refinement for faster rates. The core idea is to control the generalization gap by analyzing roundwise selector-loss information terms.
data_sources: The paper doesn't explicitly mention specific financial data sources. However, the methods are applicable to online learning, streaming active learning, and stochastic multi-armed bandits, which could potentially use financial time series data, order book data, or news feeds.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential arises from improved model generalization in dynamic market environments. By providing tighter generalization bounds for online learning algorithms, the research could lead to more robust and adaptive trading strategies. This is especially relevant for strategies that need to continuously learn and adapt to changing market conditions, such as those using reinforcement learning or adaptive portfolio optimization.

title: Multi-Task Representation Learning for Conservative Linear Bandits
summary: This paper presents the Constrained Multi-Task Representation Learning (CMTRL) framework for linear bandits. We consider T linear bandit tasks in a d dimensional space, which share a common low-dimensional representation of dimension r, where r is much smaller than the minimum of d and T. Furthermore, tasks are constrained so that only actions meeting specific safety or performance requirements are allowed, referred to as conservative (safe) bandits. We introduce a novel algorithm, Safe-Alternating projected Gradient Descent and minimization (Safe-AltGDmin), to recover a low-rank feature matrix while satisfying the given constraints. Building on this algorithm, we propose a multi-task representation learning framework for conservative linear bandits and establish theoretical guarantees for its regret and sample complexity bounds. We presented experiments and compared the performance of our algorithm with benchmark algorithms.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Constrained Multi-Task Representation Learning (CMTRL) framework using Safe-Alternating projected Gradient Descent and minimization (Safe-AltGDmin) to address linear bandit problems with safety constraints. It aims to learn a common low-dimensional representation across multiple related tasks, which can be interpreted as learning shared factor exposures within a market.
data_sources: The abstract doesn't explicitly specify data sources, but implicitly it is meant to be sequential decision-making with rewards generated from a linear structure, meaning market data or perhaps even simulated market data could be ingested. The key is its application in learning factors.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential stems from more efficient exploration and exploitation in a multi-task setting with safety constraints. In trading, 'tasks' could represent different assets, market regimes, or trading styles. Safety constraints can be interpreted as risk limits or minimum acceptable Sharpe ratios, meaning the algorithm can learn more quickly while respecting risk management.
title_cn: 保守线性Bandit算法的多任务表征学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种保守多任务表征学习框架，可应用于量化交易中。其核心思想是在满足安全约束（如风险限制）的前提下，跨不同资产或市场状态学习共享的低维因子表示。 通过更高效地探索和利用多任务信息，该算法有望加速交易策略的训练和优化，同时保证风险可控。适用于学习高维资产的因子模型。

title: MM-OptBench: A Solver-Grounded Benchmark for Multimodal Optimization Modeling
summary: Optimization modeling translates real decision-making problems into mathematical optimization models and solver-executable implementations. Although language models are increasingly used to generate optimization formulations and solver code, existing benchmarks are almost entirely text-only. This omits many optimization-modeling tasks that arise in operational practice, where requirements are described in text but instance information is conveyed through visual artifacts such as tables, graphs, maps, schedules, and dashboards. We introduce multimodal optimization modeling, a benchmark setting in which models must construct both a mathematical formulation and executable solver code from a text-and-visual problem specification. To evaluate this setting, we develop a solver-grounded framework that generates structured optimization instances, verifies each with an exact solver, and builds both the model-facing inputs and hidden reference files from the same verified source. We instantiate the framework as MM-OptBench, a benchmark of 780 solver-verified instances spanning 6 optimization families, 26 subcategories, and 3 structural difficulty levels. We evaluate 9 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), including 6 frontier general-purpose models and 3 math-specialized models, with aggregate, family-level, difficulty-level, and failure-mode analyses. The results show that the task remains far from solved: the best two models reach 52.1% and 51.3% pass@1, while on average across the six general-purpose MLLMs, pass@1 is 43.4% on easy instances and 15.9% on hard instances. All three math-specialized MLLMs solve 0/780 instances. Failure attribution shows that errors arise both when extracting instance data from text and visuals and when turning extracted data into solver-correct formulations and code. MM-OptBench provides a testbed for solver-grounded, decision-oriented multimodal intelligence.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MM-OptBench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in generating optimization models and solver code from text and visual inputs. It uses a solver-grounded framework to create verified optimization instances, covering various optimization families and difficulty levels. The evaluation involves testing MLLMs' ability to extract information and formulate solver-correct code.
data_sources: The benchmark dataset is constructed to contain instances across different families of mathematical optimization problems, with instance information represented via text and visual artifacts (tables, graphs). Specific market data is not used, as the focus is on the generation of optimization models.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in automating the process of creating and adapting optimization models from real-world data sources. While the paper doesn't directly propose a trading strategy, improved MLLMs could automate the adaptation of portfolio optimization or resource allocation models to incorporate new data (e.g., sentiment from news articles, supply chain disruptions visualized as graphs) with less human intervention. This could potentially lead to more adaptive and efficient trading strategies. However, the current state of MLLMs in this area is not sufficient for direct deployment.
title_cn: MM-OptBench：一个基于求解器的多模态优化建模基准
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一个用于评估多模态大型语言模型在生成优化模型和求解器代码方面的基准。利用文本和视觉信息，自动构建数学规划模型并生成求解代码，可用于更高效地将非结构化数据转化为可执行的交易策略，比如从新闻和供应链信息中动态调整投资组合，尽管目前技术尚不成熟。

title: BoolXLLM: LLM-Assisted Explainability for Boolean Models
summary:
Interpretable machine learning aims to provide transparent models whose decision-making processes can be readily understood by humans. Recent advances in rule-based approaches, such as expressive Boolean formulas (BoolXAI), offer faithful and compact representations of model behavior. However, for non-technical stakeholders, main challenges remain in practice: (i) selecting semantically meaningful features and (ii) translating formal logical rules into accessible explanations.
  In this work, we propose BoolXLLM , as a hybrid framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) into the end-to-end pipeline of Boolean rule learning. We augment BoolXAI , an expressive Boolean rule-based classifier, with LLMs at three critical stages: (1) feature selection, where LLMs guide the identification of domain-relevant variables; (2) threshold recommendation, where LLMs propose semantically meaningful discretization strategies for numerical features; and (3) rule compression and interpretation, where Boolean rules are translated into natural language explanations at both global and local levels.
  This integration bridges formal, faithful explanations with human-understandable narratives. This allows build an explainable AI system that is both theoretically grounded and accessible to non-experts. Early empirical results demonstrate that LLM-assisted pipelines improve interpretability while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Our work highlights the promise of combining symbolic reasoning with language-based models for human-centered explainability.
core_methodology: The paper introduces BoolXLLM, a hybrid framework that combines Boolean rule learning (BoolXAI) with Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve interpretability of rule-based classifiers. The LLMs are used for feature selection, threshold recommendation for numerical features, and translating logical rules into natural language explanations. The goal is to make interpretable AI systems more accessible to non-experts.
data_sources: The abstract does not explicitly mention specific financial data sources. However, the methodology is generic and applicable to any dataset with features that can be used in Boolean rule learning. In a financial context, this could include price and volume data, technical indicators, or fundamental data.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in identifying interpretable trading rules that are easily understood and explainable. By using LLMs to simplify the interpretation of Boolean rules, traders can potentially gain more confidence in complex models and better understand their behavior. The system can find novel combinations of features, previously obscured or requiring in-depth domain-specific knowledge to identify. The interpretability could also allow for improved risk management and more informed trading decisions avoiding black-box errors of deep learning models.
title_cn: BoolXLLM：基于LLM的布尔模型可解释性
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结合布尔规则学习和大型语言模型（LLM）的混合框架BoolXLLM，旨在提高规则型分类器的可解释性。LLM用于特征选择、数值特征阈值推荐以及将逻辑规则转换为自然语言解释。这种方法可以帮助交易者更好地理解交易模型的行为，发现新颖的特征组合，降低风险，并做出更明智的交易决策。

title: Large Language Models as Amortized Pareto-Front Generators for Constrained Bi-Objective Convex Optimization
summary: Generating feasible Pareto fronts for constrained bi-objective continuous optimization is central to multi-criteria decision-making. Existing methods usually rely on iterative scalarization, evolutionary search, or problem-specific solvers, requiring repeated optimization for each instance. We introduce DIPS, an end-to-end framework that fine-tunes large language models as amortized Pareto-front generators for constrained bi-objective convex optimization. Given a textual problem description, DIPS directly outputs an ordered set of feasible continuous decision vectors approximating the Pareto front. To make continuous optimization compatible with autoregressive language modeling, DIPS combines a compact discretization scheme, Numerically Grounded Token Initialization for new numerical tokens, and Three-Phase Curriculum Optimization, which progressively aligns structural validity, feasibility, and Pareto-front quality. Across five families of constrained bi-objective convex problems, a fine-tuned 7B-parameter model achieves normalized hypervolume ratios of 95.29% to 98.18% relative to reference fronts. With vLLM-accelerated inference, DIPS solves one instance in as little as 0.16 seconds and outperforms general-purpose and reasoning LLM baselines under the evaluated setting. These results suggest that LLMs can serve as effective amortized generators for continuous Pareto-front approximation.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DIPS, a framework that fine-tunes Large Language Models (LLMs) to directly generate Pareto fronts for constrained bi-objective convex optimization problems. It utilizes a compact discretization scheme, Numerically Grounded Token Initialization, and a Three-Phase Curriculum Optimization to align validity, feasibility, and Pareto-front quality. The LLM takes a textual problem description as input and outputs a set of decision vectors approximating the Pareto front.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the model on five families of constrained bi-objective convex problems. While the paper doesn't explicitly use financial data, the optimization problem type can be mapped to various financial scenarios like portfolio optimization with multiple objectives and constraints.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in using LLMs to quickly generate near-optimal solutions for complex portfolio optimization or asset allocation problems with multiple objectives (e.g., maximizing return, minimizing risk, minimizing transaction costs). The speed of the LLM-based solution (0.16 seconds) offers an advantage for rapid rebalancing or adaptation to changing market conditions. Furthermore, exploring different problem descriptions (e.g., incorporating sentiment or news data) could potentially uncover novel investment strategies. The amortized nature of solving the problem offers computational efficiency compared to traditional optimization methods.
title_cn: 大型语言模型作为约束双目标凸优化问题的分摊帕累托前沿生成器
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种利用大型语言模型（LLM）快速生成约束双目标凸优化问题帕累托前沿的框架DIPS。该方法可应用于多目标投资组合优化，例如在考虑收益、风险和交易成本的约束下，快速找到最优资产配置方案。相比传统优化方法，DIPS具有更快的求解速度，可在市场快速变化时进行快速调整。通过引入新的问题描述(如情绪或新闻数据)，可能发现新型投资策略。

title: Elicitation-Augmented Bayesian Optimization
summary: Human-in-the-loop Bayesian optimization (HITL BO) methods utilize human expertise to improve the sample-efficiency of BO. Most HITL BO methods assume that a domain expert can quantify their knowledge, for instance by pinpointing query locations or specifying their prior beliefs about the location of the maximum as a probability distribution. However, since human expertise is often tacit and cannot be explicitly quantified, we consider a setting where domain knowledge of an expert is elicited via pairwise comparisons of designs. We interpret the expert's pairwise judgements as noisy evidence about the values of the observable objective function and develop a principled method for combining the information obtained via direct observations and pairwise queries. Specifically, we derive a cost-aware value-of-information acquisition function that balances direct observations against pairwise queries. The proposed method approaches the convex hull of the trajectories of the individual information sources: when pairwise queries are cheap it substantially improves sample-efficiency over observation-only BO, and when pairwise queries are costly or noisy, it recovers the performance of standard BO by relying on direct observations alone.
core_methodology: Elicitation-Augmented Bayesian Optimization, which combines direct observations of an objective function with noisy pairwise comparisons elicited from human experts. The acquisition function is cost-aware, balancing the trade-off between direct observations and expert queries. It aims to improve sample efficiency by leveraging human expertise when available and cost-effective.
data_sources: The paper focuses on a general framework, so the specific data sources are not explicitly defined. In financial applications, these could be market data (price, volume, order book) used in parameter optimization for trading strategies, or alternative data where human judgment can inform the process (e.g., sentiment analysis).
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in the efficient optimization of trading strategy parameters or the incorporation of qualitative expert knowledge into model building. For example, if a momentum strategy's parameters are optimized using this method, the human expert could provide insights about market conditions that affect the strategy's performance, leading to better parameter selection and improved risk-adjusted returns. Furthermore, using expert pairwise comparisons might offer a structured manner of including sentiment or subjective indicators, which are traditionally difficult to model quantitatively.
title_cn: 启发式增强贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: 该方法通过结合直接观测和专家知识，更有效地优化交易策略参数。专家通过成对比较提供市场见解，帮助模型选择更优参数，提高策略的风险调整收益。适用于量化策略的参数寻优，也可用于整合难以量化的市场情绪等因素。

title: Limits of Learning Linear Dynamics from Experiments
summary: Learning governing dynamics from data is a common goal across the sciences, yet it is only well-posed when the underlying mechanisms are identifiable. In practice, many data-driven methods implicitly assume identifiability; when this assumption fails, estimated models can yield spurious predictions and invalid mechanistic conclusions. Classical identifiability guarantees for controlled linear time-invariant (LTI) systems provide sufficient conditions -- controllability and persistent excitation -- but leave open whether identifiability holds when these conditions fail, and which parts of the system remain identifiable without full identifiability. We show that the experimental setup, i.e., the realized initial state and control input, dictates a fundamental limit on the information recoverable from the observed trajectory. We develop a geometric characterization of this limit and derive a closed-form description of all systems consistent with the experimental setup. Crucially, we prove that even when the full system is not identifiable, the restricted dynamics on the subspace reachable by the experiment remain uniquely determined.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on the identifiability limitations of learning linear time-invariant (LTI) system dynamics from experimental data. It provides a geometric characterization of the unidentifiable subspace and derives a closed-form description of systems consistent with the data.  A key result is that even when the full system dynamics are not identifiable, the dynamics restricted to the reachable subspace are uniquely determined by the experiment.
data_sources: The analysis is theoretical; example data would consist of state and control trajectories from a dynamical system, such as price and order flow data in a limit order book.
alpha_potential: While not directly providing an alpha generation method, the paper is relevant for building more robust models for market microstructure and optimal execution. Specifically, it offers a framework to understand and mitigate the effects of partial observability when learning market dynamics from data. For instance, one could apply the principles to build state-space models of order book dynamics or use the identifiability analysis to constrain parameters in a reduced-form model. Moreover, this can guide experiment design for reinforcement learning agents involved in trading, optimizing exploration for full system identification.
title_cn: 从实验中学习线性动态的局限性
summary_cn: 该论文研究了从实验数据中学习线性时不变系统动态的局限性。它提供了一种几何表征，用于描述不可识别的子空间，并推导出与数据一致的系统的闭式描述。即使完整系统动态无法识别，在可达子空间上的受限动态也是唯一确定的。 这对于构建更强大的市场微观结构模型和优化交易执行具有重要意义，并指导强化学习智能体进行实验设计。

title: Estimating Subgraph Importance with Structural Prior Domain Knowledge
summary: We propose a subgraph importance estimation method for pretrained Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) on graph-level tasks, formulated as a linear Group Lasso regression problem in the embedding space. Our method effectively leverages prior domain knowledge of graph substructures, while remaining independent of the specific form of the output layer or readout function used in the GNN architecture, and it does not require access to ground-truth target labels. Experiments on real-world graph datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing baselines in subgraph importance estimation. Furthermore, we extend our method to identify important nodes within the graph.
core_methodology: The paper presents a method to estimate subgraph importance in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) using a Group Lasso regression approach in the embedding space. It leverages prior domain knowledge of graph substructures to identify critical components and nodes within the graph, independent of the output layer or readout function and without needing ground-truth labels.  The approach aims to improve the interpretability of GNNs applied to graph-level tasks.
data_sources: The abstract mentions experiments on real-world graph datasets but doesn't specify the exact nature of these datasets.  The kind of graphs used are more likely social or biological networks rather than financial networks, but the method is fairly general.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in identifying important relationships or patterns within complex financial networks. For example, identifying key nodes in a network of companies can help in understanding systemic risk. Applying this to order book graphs might reveal hidden order imbalances or manipulative tactics.  Understanding these 'important' subgraphs could provide an edge in predicting price movements or identifying arbitrage opportunities.
title_cn: 利用结构先验领域知识估计子图重要性
summary_cn: 该论文提出一种利用图神经网络（GNN）估计子图重要性的方法。通过在嵌入空间中应用Group Lasso回归，并结合结构先验知识，识别关键子图和节点。该方法可应用于金融网络，例如公司关系网络，供应链网络，甚至高频订单薄中的关系。通过识别这些重要关系，可以预测价格波动、发现套利机会或评估系统性风险，从而指导量化交易策略。

title: Split the Differences, Pool the Rest: Provably Efficient Multi-Objective Imitation
summary: This work investigates multi-objective imitation learning: the problem of recovering policies that lie on the Pareto front given demonstrations from multiple Pareto-optimal experts in a Multi-Objective Markov Decision Process (MOMDP). Standard imitation approaches are ill-equipped for this regime, as naively aggregating conflicting expert trajectories can result in dominated policies. To address this, we introduce Multi-Output Augmented Behavioral Cloning (MA-BC), an algorithm that systematically partitions divergent expert data while pooling state-action pairs where no behavior conflict is observed. Theoretically, we prove that MA-BC converges to Pareto-optimal policies at a faster statistical rate than any learner that considers each expert dataset independently. Furthermore, we establish a novel lower bound for multi-objective imitation learning, demonstrating that MA-BC is minimax optimal. Finally, we empirically validate our algorithm across diverse discrete environments and, guided by our theoretical insights, extend and evaluate MA-BC on a continuous Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control task.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Multi-Output Augmented Behavioral Cloning (MA-BC) for multi-objective imitation learning. It addresses the problem of learning Pareto-optimal policies from demonstrations by multiple experts with conflicting objectives. The algorithm partitions expert data where behaviors diverge and pools data where behaviors align. The key novelty lies in its ability to balance multiple objectives simultaneously.
data_sources: The paper uses diverse discrete environments and a continuous Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control task for empirical validation. While not explicitly financial data, the methodology could be adapted to learn from multiple market participants with conflicting objectives (e.g., high-frequency traders versus long-term investors).
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in the ability to learn robust strategies that balance multiple potentially conflicting objectives in financial markets. For example, it could be used to create a portfolio that optimizes for both return and risk by learning from the actions of different fund managers who prioritize different objectives. Another area is in order execution, where the objective can be minimizing market impact but also maximizing execution speed.
title_cn: 拆分差异，合并剩余：可证明高效的多目标模仿学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种名为多输出增强行为克隆（MA-BC）的算法，用于解决多目标模仿学习问题，旨在从多个具有冲突目标的专家的演示中学习帕累托最优策略。该方法通过区分不同行为的专家数据，并合并一致行为的数据，从而在金融市场中平衡多个相互冲突的目标，例如优化风险回报或兼顾执行速度和市场冲击。

title: Stochastic Minimum-Cost Reach-Avoid Reinforcement Learning
summary: We study stochastic minimum-cost reach-avoid reinforcement learning, where an agent must satisfy a reach-avoid specification with probability at least $p$ while minimizing expected cumulative costs in stochastic environments. Existing safe and constrained reinforcement learning methods typically fail to jointly enforce probabilistic reach-avoid constraints and optimize cost in the learning setting in stochastic environments. To address this challenge, we introduce reach-avoid probability certificates (RAPCs), which identify states from which stochastic reach-avoid constraints are satisfiable. Building on RAPCs, we develop a contraction-based Bellman formulation that serves as a principled surrogate for integrating reach-avoid considerations into reinforcement learning, enabling cost optimization under probabilistic constraints. We establish almost sure convergence of the proposed algorithms to locally optimal policies with respect to the resulting objective. Experiments in the MuJoCo simulator demonstrate improved cost performance and consistently higher reach-avoid satisfaction rates.
core_methodology: The paper introduces reach-avoid probability certificates (RAPCs) and a contraction-based Bellman formulation to integrate probabilistic reach-avoid constraints into reinforcement learning. The method aims to minimize expected cumulative costs while satisfying probabilistic constraints, enabling cost optimization under these constraints in stochastic environments.
data_sources: Experiments are conducted in the MuJoCo simulator, which is not directly financial market data. Application to financial markets would require adaptation using historical market data, order book information, and potentially news feeds or sentiment data.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in developing trading strategies that need to satisfy certain risk constraints probabilistically. For example, a strategy could aim to maximize profit while ensuring a high probability of avoiding large drawdowns or of reaching a profit target within a specific timeframe. Applying this methodology could lead to improved risk-adjusted returns by explicitly incorporating risk management into the learning process. For instance, one could frame market making as a reach-avoid problem: reach a certain inventory level while avoiding excessive exposure. Or one can optimize for a target PnL with a constraint to avoid ruin.
title_cn: 随机最小成本到达-规避强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的强化学习方法，旨在满足概率性的到达-规避约束，同时最小化预期累积成本。通过引入到达-规避概率证书（RAPC）和基于压缩的贝尔曼公式，使算法能够在随机环境中优化策略，并确保高概率满足预设约束。在交易应用中，该方法可用于开发在满足特定风险约束（如避免大幅回撤）的前提下最大化利润的策略。

title: Assessing and Mitigating Miscalibration in LLM-Based Social Science Measurement
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in social science as scalable measurement tools for converting unstructured text into variables that can enter standard empirical designs. Measurement validity demands more than high average accuracy, which requires well calibrated confidence that faithfully reflects the empirical probability of each measurement being correct. This paper studies the model miscalibration in LLM-based social science measurement. We begin with a case study on FOMC and show that confidence based filtering can change downstream regression estimates when LLM confidence is miscalibrated. We then audit calibration across 14 social science constructs covering both proprietary models, including GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2, and open source models. Across tasks and model families, reported confidence is poorly aligned with tolerance-based correctness. As a simple mitigation, we propose a soft label distillation pipeline for calibrating Bert with LLM. The method converts an LLM score and its verbalized confidence into a soft target distribution, then trains a smaller discriminative classifier on encoder models for these targets. Averaged across datasets, this approach reduces ECE by 43.2\% and Brier by 34.0\%. These results suggest that LLM-based social science pipelines should treat calibration as part of measurement validity, rather than as an optional post-processing concern.
core_methodology: The paper investigates the miscalibration of Large Language Models (LLMs) in social science measurement, particularly focusing on the confidence scores provided by these models. It finds that LLM confidence is often poorly aligned with actual correctness. To mitigate this, the authors propose a soft label distillation pipeline using a smaller BERT model trained on the LLM's outputs (score and verbalized confidence). This calibration method aims to improve the reliability of LLM-based measurements.
data_sources: The research uses the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) statements as a case study and also audits calibration across 14 social science constructs. The paper utilizes outputs from both proprietary (GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2) and open-source LLMs.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in improving sentiment analysis or topic extraction related to financial news, economic indicators, or company reports. By calibrating LLM confidence, traders can potentially filter out unreliable signals derived from unstructured text data. For example, improved extraction of sentiment from FOMC statements or earnings call transcripts could provide a more precise view of market sentiment and inform trading decisions. More reliable classification of economic reports can provide improved predictions and hence alpha.
title_cn: 评估和缓解基于LLM的社会科学测量中的校准误差
summary_cn: 该研究发现大型语言模型在社会科学测量中存在校准误差，即模型置信度与实际准确性不符。作者提出一种软标签蒸馏方法，利用BERT模型校准LLM的输出，从而提高从金融新闻、经济指标和公司报告等非结构化文本中提取情绪或主题的可靠性，为量化交易提供更精确的信号。

title: Delightful Gradients Accelerate Corner Escape
summary: Softmax policy gradient converges at $O(1/t)$, but its transient behavior near sub-optimal corners of the simplex can be exponentially slow. The bottleneck is self-trapping: negative-advantage actions reinforce the corner policy and can initially push the optimal action backward. We study \emph{Delightful Policy Gradient} (DG), which gates each policy-gradient term by the product of advantage and action surprisal. For $K$-armed bandits, we prove that the zero-temperature limit of DG removes this corner-trapping mechanism on a quantitative sector near any sub-optimal corner, yielding a first-exit escape bound logarithmic in the initial probability ratio. At every fixed temperature, the same local mechanism persists because harmful actions are polynomially suppressed as they become rare. A key structural insight is that every action better than the corner action is an \emph{ally}: its contribution to escape is non-negative. Combining corner instability with a monotonic value improvement identity, we prove that DG converges globally to the optimal policy in both bandits and tabular MDPs at an asymptotic $O(1/t)$ rate. We also show, via an exact counterexample, that this tabular mechanism can fail under shared function approximation. In MNIST contextual bandits with a shared-parameter neural network, DG nevertheless recovers from bad initializations faster than standard policy gradient, suggesting that the counterexample marks a boundary of the theory rather than a practical prohibition.
core_methodology: The paper introduces 'Delightful Policy Gradient' (DG), a modification to the standard softmax policy gradient in reinforcement learning. DG gates each policy-gradient term by the product of advantage and action surprisal. This aims to mitigate the self-trapping behavior near sub-optimal corners in policy space, which can hinder convergence. Theoretical analysis and experiments on K-armed bandits and tabular MDPs demonstrate improved escape from these 'corners' and faster convergence to the optimal policy. Tests on MNIST contextual bandits suggest robustness to function approximation.
data_sources: The paper uses synthetic data from K-armed bandits and tabular MDP environments. It also includes an experiment with MNIST contextual bandits, which implicitly uses image data.
alpha_potential: Potential alpha sources arise from improved exploration-exploitation balance in reinforcement learning agents that are used for dynamic order execution, portfolio optimization, or market making. By escaping local optima more efficiently, DG could enable RL agents to discover more profitable trading strategies faster than standard policy gradient algorithms. The faster convergence to the optimum is the key.
title_cn: 愉悦梯度加速逃离困境
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种改进的策略梯度算法“愉悦梯度(DG)”，旨在解决强化学习在接近次优策略时陷入局部最优的问题。DG通过优势函数和行为意外性的乘积来调整梯度，从而加速算法跳出局部最优。DG可能应用于动态订单执行、投资组合优化或做市策略，从而提高交易agent发现更优策略的速度。

title: Incentivizing Truthfulness and Collaborative Fairness in Bayesian Learning
summary: Collaborative machine learning involves training high-quality models using datasets from a number of sources. To incentivize sources to share data, existing data valuation methods fairly reward each source based on its data submitted as is. However, as these methods do not verify nor incentivize data truthfulness, the sources can manipulate their data (e.g., by submitting duplicated or noisy data) to artificially increase their valuations and rewards or prevent others from benefiting. This paper presents the first mechanism that provably ensures (F) collaborative fairness and incentivizes (T) truthfulness at equilibrium for Bayesian models. Our mechanism combines semivalues (e.g., Shapley value), which ensure fairness, and a truthful data valuation function (DVF) based on a validation set that is unknown to the sources. As semivalues are influenced by others' data, we introduce an additional condition to prove that a source can maximize its expected data values in coalitions and semivalues by submitting a dataset that captures its true knowledge. Additionally, we discuss the implications and suitable relaxations of (F) and (T) when the mediator has a limited budget for rewards or lacks a validation set. Our theoretical findings are validated on synthetic and real-world datasets.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a mechanism combining semivalues (like Shapley value) for fairness and a truthful data valuation function (DVF) that uses a validation set unseen by the data providers. This aims to incentivize truthful data sharing in collaborative Bayesian learning. The key idea is to reward data providers based on the value of their data, while discouraging manipulation by ensuring that the best strategy is to submit truthful data.
data_sources: The paper validates the mechanism on both synthetic and real-world datasets making the applicability broad. While real-world datasets aren't financial specific, the methodology opens the door for utilizing market or alternative data where quality and veracity are questionable.
alpha_potential: The main alpha potential lies in improving data quality and leveraging better-trained models. Specifically, by incentivizing truthful data submission in fragmented or decentralized data environments in financial markets. Examples include datasets from various brokers/exchanges or even sentiment data. Clean and truthful validated data can provide improved model performance and reduce spurious signals that lead to losing trades.
title_cn: 贝叶斯学习中激励真实性和协同公平性的机制
summary_cn: 本文提出一种新机制，通过结合 Shapley 值等半值方法和基于验证集的真实数据估值函数，激励参与者在协同贝叶斯学习中提供真实数据。该机制旨在解决数据质量问题，通过奖励真实数据的贡献者，提高模型训练质量和有效性。可应用于金融市场中数据分散的场景，减少因数据失真导致的错误交易信号。

title: Sobolev Regularized MMD Gradient Flow
summary: We propose Sobolev-regularized Maximum Mean Discrepancy (SrMMD) gradient flow, a regularized variant of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) gradient flow based on a gradient penalty on the witness function. The proposed regularization mitigates the non-convexity of the MMD objective and yields provable \emph{global} convergence guarantees in MMD in both continuous and discrete time. A more surprising appeal is that our convergence analysis does not rely on isoperimetric assumptions on the target distribution. Instead, it is based on a regularity condition on the difference between kernel mean embeddings. A key highlight of the proposed flow is that it is applicable in both sampling (from an unnormalized target distribution) -- using Stein kernels -- and generative modeling settings, unlike previous works, where a gradient flow is suitable for only generative modeling or sampling but not both. The effectiveness of the proposed flow is empirically verified on a broad range of tasks in both generative modelling and sampling.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Sobolev-regularized Maximum Mean Discrepancy (SrMMD) gradient flow for both sampling from unnormalized distributions and generative modeling. It uses a gradient penalty on the witness function to improve convergence and applies Stein kernels. The key improvement is its applicability to both sampling and generative tasks, unlike previous methods that are suitable for only one.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but potentially can be applied on financial time series data to generate synthetic data or to estimate distributions.
alpha_potential: Could potentially be used for anomaly detection (identifying out-of-distribution market behavior), generating synthetic financial data for backtesting robustness, or for option pricing where calibrated distributions are critical. The ability to sample from and learn complex distributions faster and more reliably could lead to better risk management and model calibration.
title_cn: 索博列夫正则化最大均值差异梯度流
summary_cn: 该论文提出一种改进的最大均值差异(MMD)梯度流方法，可用于生成模型和从未知分布中采样。在金融领域，此方法可能用于生成更真实的合成市场数据，用于压力测试和风险管理， 或用于更精确地估计期权定价中的标的资产分布，从而提高定价模型的准确性和增强风险控制能力。

title: Constrained Stochastic Spectral Preconditioning Converges for Nonconvex Objectives
summary: In this work, we develop proximal preconditioned gradient methods with a focus on spectral gradient methods providing a proximal extension to the Muon and Scion optimizers. We introduce a family of stochastic algorithms that can handle a wide variety of convex and nonconvex constraints and study its convergence under heavy-tailed noise, through a novel analysis tailored to the geometry of the proposed methods. We further propose a variance-reduced version, which achieves faster convergence under standard noise assumptions. Finally, we show that the polynomial iterations used in Muon are more accurately captured by a nonlinear preconditioner than by the ideal matrix sign, leading to a convergence analysis that more faithfully reflects practical implementations.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a family of stochastic, proximal preconditioned gradient methods, focusing on spectral gradient approaches. It extends Muon and Scion optimizers and analyzes convergence under heavy-tailed noise with a variance-reduced version for faster convergence. It refines the analysis of polynomial iterations in Muon using a nonlinear preconditioner.
data_sources: While the paper itself doesn't explicitly mention data sources, its algorithms can be applied to various financial data including price series, order book data, and potentially alternative datasets for model training and optimization.
alpha_potential: Potential alpha generation lies in more efficiently training complex models used in quantitative finance. The improved convergence, especially under heavy-tailed noise, suggests more robust parameter estimation for models that capture market dynamics. Faster training allows for more frequent model recalibration, potentially capturing transient market inefficiencies. Preconditioning could also stabilize training for models with high dimensionality or ill-conditioned optimization landscapes, common in portfolio optimization and risk management.
title_cn: 非凸目标约束下的随机谱预处理收敛
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种针对非凸目标的约束随机谱预处理梯度优化算法，旨在提高模型训练的效率和鲁棒性。通过改进的梯度下降算法，该方法加速了复杂金融模型（如投资组合优化、风险管理模型）的参数估计过程，使其能更快地适应市场变化，挖掘潜在的交易机会。

title: Minimax Rates and Spectral Distillation for Tree Ensembles
summary: Tree ensembles such as random forests (RFs) and gradient boosting machines (GBMs) are among the most widely used supervised learners, yet their theoretical properties remain incompletely understood. We adopt a spectral perspective on these algorithms, with two main contributions. First, we derive minimax-optimal convergence for RF regression, showing that, under mild regularity conditions on tree growth, the eigenvalue decay of the induced kernel operator governs the statistical rate. Second, we exploit this spectral viewpoint to develop compression schemes for tree ensembles. For RFs, leading eigenfunctions of the kernel operator capture the dominant predictive directions; for GBMs, leading singular vectors of the smoother matrix play an analogous role. Learning nonlinear maps for these spectral representations yields distilled models that are orders of magnitude smaller than the originals while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Our methods compare favorably to state of the art algorithms for forest pruning and rule extraction, with applications to resource constrained computing.
core_methodology: The paper provides a spectral perspective on tree ensembles (Random Forests and Gradient Boosting Machines), deriving minimax-optimal convergence rates and developing compression schemes (spectral distillation) to create smaller, faster models while maintaining predictive performance. This involves analyzing the eigenvalue/singular vector decay of kernel operators and smoother matrices associated with the ensembles to identify dominant predictive directions.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular datasets; the proposed methods are applicable to various regression problems, including those found in financial markets (e.g., predicting asset returns or volatility). However, backtesting with relevant market data would be required to assess its utility.
alpha_potential: The spectral distillation approach, by creating smaller and faster tree ensemble models, can improve model deployment speed and memory efficiency, potentially enabling higher-frequency trading strategies. The identification of dominant predictive directions could also lead to feature selection or improved signal extraction strategies when combined with alternative data sources.
title_cn: 树集成模型的极小极大速率和谱蒸馏
summary_cn: 该论文从谱分析角度研究了树集成模型，提出了谱蒸馏压缩算法，可以在保持预测性能的同时大幅减小模型体积，提升计算效率。该方法应用于金融市场，可以通过更快速度的模型进行交易决策，或者利用提取的特征优化信号生成，提升策略能力。

title: Gradient Clipping Beyond Vector Norms: A Spectral Approach for Matrix-Valued Parameters
summary: Gradient clipping is a standard safeguard for training neural networks under noisy, heavy-tailed stochastic gradients; yet, most clipping rules treat all parameters as vectors and ignore the matrix structure of modern architectures. We show empirically that data outliers often amplify only a small number of leading singular values in layer-wise gradient matrices, while the rest of the spectrum remains largely unchanged. Motivated by this phenomenon, we propose spectral clipping, which stabilizes training by clamping singular values that exceed a threshold while preserving the singular directions. This framework generalizes classical gradient norm clipping and can be easily integrated into existing optimizers. We provide a convergence analysis for non-convex optimization with spectrally clipped SGD, yielding the optimal $\mathcal{O}\left(K^{\frac{2 - 2α}{3α- 2}}\right)$ rate for heavy-tailed noise. To minimize hyperparameter tuning, we introduce layer-wise adaptive thresholds based on moving averages or sliding-window quantiles of the top singular values. Finally, we develop efficient implementations that clip only the top $r$ singular values via randomized truncated SVD, avoiding full decompositions for large layers. We demonstrate competitive performance across synthetic heavy-tailed settings and neural network training tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a spectral gradient clipping method using randomized truncated SVD to stabilize training of neural networks with matrix-valued parameters under heavy-tailed noise. It focuses on clipping the leading singular values of gradient matrices that exceed a threshold, preserving singular directions. Layer-wise adaptive thresholds based on moving averages or sliding-window quantiles of the top singular values are also implemented to reduce hyperparameter tuning.
data_sources: The paper demonstrates performance on synthetic heavy-tailed settings and neural network training tasks, suggesting applicability to various datasets relevant in training ML models within Finance.
alpha_potential: The improved training stability from spectral clipping may allow for more robust and reliable financial models that are trained on noisy or outlier-ridden financial data. Specifically, this method can aid in training more effective predictive models for asset prices, volatility, or other financial indicators where outliers can significantly affect training.

title: Automated Reformulation of Robust Optimization via Memory-Augmented Large Language Models
summary: Robust optimization (RO) provides a principled framework for decision-making under uncertainty, but its practical use is often limited by the need to manually reformulate uncertain optimization models into tractable deterministic counterparts. Recent large language models (LLMs) have been shown promising for automating optimization formulation, yet RO reformulation remains challenging because it requires precise multi-step reasoning and mathematically consistent transformations. To facilitate systematic evaluation of LLM-based reformulation, for which no dedicated benchmark currently exists, we develop AutoRO-Bench, a benchmark featuring an automated data generation pipeline for the core RO reformulation task and a curated dataset for the RO application task. To address the reformulation challenge, we propose Automated Reformulation with Experience Memory (AutoREM), a tuning-free memory-augmented framework that autonomously builds a structured textual experience memory by reflecting on past failed trajectories through a tailored offline adaptation procedure. AutoREM requires neither domain-specific expert knowledge nor parameter updates, and the resulting memory readily transfers across different base LLMs. Experimental results show that AutoREM consistently improves the accuracy and efficiency of RO reformulation across in-distribution datasets, out-of-distribution datasets, and diverse base LLMs.
core_methodology: The paper presents AutoREM, a memory-augmented large language model (LLM) framework for automatically reformulating robust optimization problems. It builds a textual experience memory from past failed reformulations and uses this memory to improve the accuracy and efficiency of future reformulations. The framework is tuning-free and transfers across different base LLMs.
data_sources: The paper introduces AutoRO-Bench, a benchmark for RO reformulation, with automated data generation and a curated dataset for RO applications. Specific financial datasets are not mentioned, implying the potential need for adaptation to particular financial use cases.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential is indirect. By automating and improving the reformulation of robust optimization problems, this method can potentially enable more efficient implementation of robust portfolio optimization, robust asset allocation, or hedging strategies that are robust to parameter or model uncertainty. The increased usability and efficiency of RO could lead to strategies that perform better in adverse market conditions or exploit arbitrage opportunities while managing risk more effectively. The value lies in enhancing existing risk management rather than generating novel alpha signals directly.

title: From Token to Token Pair: Efficient Prompt Compression for Large Language Models in Clinical Prediction
summary: By processing electronic health records (EHRs) as natural language sequences, large language models (LLMs) have shown potential in clinical prediction tasks such as mortality prediction and phenotyping. However, longitudinal or highly frequent EHRs often yield excessively long token sequences that result in high computational costs and even reduced performance. Existing solutions either add modules for compression or remove less important tokens, which introduce additional inference latency or risk losing clinical information. To achieve lossless compression of token sequences without additional cost or loss of performance, we propose Medical Token-Pair Encoding (MedTPE), a layered method that extends standard tokenisation for EHR sequences. MedTPE merges frequently co-occurring medical token pairs into composite tokens, providing lossless compression while preserving the computational complexity through a dependency-aware replacement strategy. Only the embeddings of the newly introduced tokens of merely 0.5-1.0% of the LLM's parameters are fine-tuned via self-supervised learning. Experiments on real-world datasets for two clinical scenarios demonstrate that MedTPE reduces input token length by up to 31% and inference latency by 34-63%, while maintaining or even improving both predictive performance and output format compliance across multiple LLMs and four clinical prediction tasks. Furthermore, MedTPE demonstrates robustness across different input context lengths and generalisability to scientific and financial domains and different languages.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Medical Token-Pair Encoding (MedTPE), a layered method for lossless compression of token sequences in Large Language Models (LLMs). It merges frequently co-occurring medical token pairs into composite tokens, fine-tuning only a small portion of the LLM's parameters via self-supervised learning. The strategy aims to reduce input token length and inference latency without losing crucial information or adding computational cost. The key is dependency-aware replacement preserving complexity.
data_sources: Real-world electronic health record (EHR) datasets.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on clinical data, the core idea of efficiently compressing sequential data using token-pair encoding could be adapted to financial time series or news feeds. Compressing and accelerating LLM inference on financial text data (e.g., news sentiment, SEC filings) could provide a speed advantage in reacting to market-moving information. The ability to maintain or improve predictive performance despite compression is crucial. It could be relevant for high-frequency trading sentiment analysis or improving the reaction time of news-based trading strategies.
title_cn: 从令牌到令牌对：用于临床预测的大型语言模型的高效提示压缩
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种名为MedTPE的高效令牌压缩方法，可用于加速大型语言模型处理金融文本数据，例如新闻和财报。通过合并频繁出现的令牌对，减少输入长度并降低延迟，可能在新闻情绪分析和高频交易策略中获得速度优势。该方法在压缩的同时保持或提高预测性能，对于提升金融市场信息反应速度具有潜力。

title: Learning Feature Encoder with Synthetic Anomalies for Weakly Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
summary: Weakly supervised graph anomaly detection aims to unveil unusual graph instances, e.g., nodes, whose behaviors significantly differ from normal ones, given only a limited number of annotated anomalies and abundant unlabeled samples. A major challenge is to learn a meaningful latent feature representation that reduces intra-class variance among normal data while remaining highly sensitive to anomalies. Although recent works have applied self-supervised feature learning for graph anomaly detection, their strategies are not specifically tailored to its unique requirements, motivating our exploration of a more domain-specific approach. In this paper, we introduce a weakly supervised graph anomaly detection method that leverages a feature learning strategy tailored for graph anomalies. Our approach is built upon a multi-task learning scheme that extracts robust feature representations through synthesized anomalies. We generate synthetic anomalies by perturbing the normal graph in various ways and assign a dedicated detection head to each anomaly type, ensuring that learned features are sensitive to potential deviations from normal patterns. Although synthetic anomalies may not perfectly replicate real-world patterns, they provide valuable auxiliary data for effective feature learnin, much like features learned from ImageNet classification transfer to downstream vision tasks. Additionally, we adopt a two-phase learning strategy: an initial warm-up phase using only synthetic samples, followed by a full-training phase integrating both tasks, to balance the influence of synthetic and real data. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our method over its competitors. Code is available at https://github.com/yj-zhou/SAWGAD.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a weakly supervised graph anomaly detection method using a multi-task learning scheme. It involves generating synthetic anomalies by perturbing normal graph data and training a model to detect these anomalies. A two-phase training approach is used: first, training on synthetic data and then fine-tuning with real and synthetic data for robust feature representation.
data_sources: Experiments are performed on public graph datasets (unspecified in abstract).  Potential applications to financial data would likely involve adapting this to financial networks constructed from stock correlations, transaction data, or order book relationships.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in identifying unusual activity in financial networks that could indicate manipulation, insider trading, or early signs of distress. By detecting anomalous nodes or subgraphs, the algorithm could provide signals for contrarian strategies or risk management.
title_cn: 基于合成异常的特征编码器学习用于弱监督图异常检测

title: Debiased Model-based Representations for Sample-efficient Continuous Control
summary: Model-based representations recently stand out as a promising framework that embeds latent dynamics information into the representations for downstream off-policy actor-critic learning. It implicitly combines the advantages of both model-free and model-based approaches while avoiding the training costs associated with model-based methods. Nevertheless, existing model-based representation methods can fail to capture sufficient information about relevant variables and can overfit to early experiences in the replay buffer. These incur biases in representation and actor-critic learning, leading to inferior performance. To address this, we propose Debiased model-based Representations for Q-learning, tagged DR.Q algorithm. DR.Q explicitly maximizes the mutual information between the representations of the current state-action pair and the next state besides minimizing their deviations, and samples transitions with faded prioritized experience replay. We evaluate DR.Q on numerous continuous control benchmarks with a single set of hyperparameters, and the results demonstrate that DR.Q can match or surpass recent strong baselines, sometimes outperforming them by a large margin. Our code is available at https://github.com/dmksjfl/DR.Q.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DR.Q, a reinforcement learning algorithm for continuous control that focuses on learning debiased model-based representations. It aims to improve sample efficiency by maximizing the mutual information between state-action pairs and the next state, while also minimizing deviations in the learned representations. The algorithm utilizes a faded prioritized experience replay mechanism to avoid overfitting to early experiences.
data_sources: The evaluation is performed on numerous continuous control benchmarks (likely simulated environments such as those used in OpenAI Gym/MuJoCo). While not directly utilizing financial market data, the underlying methodology can be adapted.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in the algorithm's ability to learn robust and sample-efficient control policies. Applying this to algorithmic trading could potentially result in faster learning of profitable strategies and better adaptation to changing market dynamics, especially when backtesting or live deployment incurs significant computational costs (limiting the number of possible iterations). Finding a suitable continuous control formulation for trading problems (e.g., optimal order execution) could be beneficial.

title: Augmented Lagrangian Method for Last-Iterate Convergence for Constrained MDPs
summary: We study policy optimization for infinite-horizon, discounted constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs). While existing theoretical guarantees typically hold for the mixture policy, deploying such a policy is computationally and memory intensive. This leads to a practical mismatch where a single (last-iterate) policy must be deployed. Recent theoretical works have thus focused on proving last-iterate convergence, but are largely limited to the tabular setting or to algorithmic variants that are rarely used in practice. To address this, we use the classic inexact augmented Lagrangian ($\texttt{AL}$) method from constrained optimization, and propose a general framework with provable last-iterate convergence for CMDPs. We first focus on the tabular setting and propose to solve the $\texttt{AL}$ sub-problem with projected Q-ascent ($\texttt{PQA}$). Combining the theoretical guarantees of $\texttt{PQA}$ and the standard $\texttt{AL}$ analysis enables us to establish global last-iterate convergence. We generalize these results to handle log-linear policies, and demonstrate that an efficient, projected variant of $\texttt{PQA}$ can achieve last-iterate convergence with comparable guarantees as prior work. Finally, we demonstrate that our framework scales to complex non-linear policies, and evaluate it on continuous control tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Augmented Lagrangian (AL) method with projected Q-ascent (PQA) to solve constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs) for policy optimization. It focuses on ensuring last-iterate convergence, meaning the single policy deployed after training performs well, unlike mixture policies. The method handles tabular settings, log-linear policies, and is demonstrated on complex non-linear policies with continuous control tasks.
data_sources: While the abstract doesn't directly mention specific financial data sources, the method is evaluated on continuous control tasks, implying it could be adapted to financial time series data, order book data, or other market-related data used for training the RL agent.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in the possibility of creating trading strategies that adhere to specific constraints (e.g., risk limits, maximum drawdown) while optimizing for return. By using CMDPs with the proposed AL and PQA method, the framework can potentially learn policies that consistently perform well in real-world deployment due to the last-iterate convergence guarantee. Finding policies satisfying complex regulatory constraints provides additional benefit.

title: Persistent and Conversational Multi-Method Explainability for Trustworthy Financial AI
summary: Financial institutions increasingly require AI explanations that are persistent, cross-validated across methods, and conversationally accessible to human decision-makers. We present an architecture for human-centered explainable AI in financial sentiment analysis that combines three contributions. First, we treat XAI artifacts -- LIME feature attributions, occlusion-based word importance scores, and saliency heatmaps -- as persistent, searchable objects in distributed S3-compatible storage with structured metadata and natural-language summaries, enabling semantic retrieval over explanation history and automatic index reconstruction after system failures. Second, we enable multi-method explanation triangulation, where a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant compares and synthesizes results from multiple XAI methods applied to the same prediction, allowing users to assess explanation robustness through natural-language dialogue. Third, we evaluate the faithfulness of generated explanations using automated checks over grounding completeness, hallucinated claims, and method-attribution behavior. We demonstrate the architecture on an EXTRA-BRAIN financial sentiment analysis pipeline using FinBERT predictions and present evaluation results showing that constrained prompting reduces hallucination rate by 36\% and increases method-attribution citations by 73\% compared to naive prompting. We discuss implications for trustworthy, human-centered AI services in regulated financial environments.
core_methodology: The paper presents an architecture for explainable AI (XAI) applied to financial sentiment analysis. It uses LIME, occlusion-based methods, and saliency heatmaps. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant is used to compare and synthesize explanations from these methods. Faithfulness is evaluated via automated checks. Primary usage is to validate and improve FinBERT.
data_sources: The system is demonstrated on an EXTRA-BRAIN financial sentiment analysis pipeline using FinBERT predictions, implying the use of text data like news articles, social media, or analyst reports.
alpha_potential: Indirect alpha potential. More trustworthy and reliable sentiment analysis models (like FinBERT after using the XAI methods to improve it) can lead to better prediction of market movements or company performance, ultimately improving profitability in sentiment-based trading strategies. Reduced hallucination in explanations can prevent incorrect interpretations and erroneous trading decisions.

title: Posterior Contraction Rates for Sparse Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Anisotropic Besov Spaces
summary: We study posterior contraction rates for sparse Bayesian Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) over anisotropic Besov spaces, providing a statistical foundation of KANs from a Bayesian point of view. We show that sparse Bayesian KANs equipped with spike-and-slab-type sparsity priors attain the near-minimax posterior contraction. In particular, the contraction rate depends on the intrinsic anisotropic smoothness of the underlying function. Moreover, by placing a hyperprior on a single model-size parameter, the resulting posterior adapts to unknown anisotropic smoothness and still achieves the corresponding near-minimax rate. A distinctive feature of our results, compared with those for standard sparse MLP-based models, is that the KAN depth can be kept fixed: owing to the flexibility of learnable spline edge functions, the required approximation complexity is controlled through the network width, spline-grid range and size, and parameter sparsity. Our analysis develops theoretical tools tailored to sparse spline-edge architectures, including approximation and complexity bounds for Bayesian KANs. We then extend to compositional Besov spaces and show that the contraction rates depend on layerwise smoothness and effective dimension of the underlying compositional structure, thereby effectively avoiding the curse of dimensionality. Together, the developed tools and findings advance the theoretical understanding of Bayesian neural networks and provide rigorous statistical foundations for KANs.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on the theoretical properties of Bayesian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), specifically their posterior contraction rates and ability to approximate functions in anisotropic Besov spaces. It establishes statistical foundations for KANs and demonstrates near-minimax posterior contraction with spike-and-slab priors. The key is the adaptive function approximation achieved through network width and spline-grid parameters.
data_sources: The paper is theoretical and does not explicitly use any specific market data. However, the methodology could be applied to any financial time series or feature set.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in the potential for KANs to learn complex, non-linear relationships in financial data and adapt to varying smoothness properties often exhibited in financial time series. Sparse Bayesian KANs might provide more robust estimations of complex, non-linear relationships than traditional MLPs due to the added regularization through the spike-and-slab prior and adaptive structure. This might translate into a better prediction of asset returns or other financial metrics, ultimately improving trading strategy performance. The ability to avoid the curse of dimensionality via compositional Besov spaces also allows the model to scale to situations with a very large feature space.

title: Learning U-Statistics with Active Inference
summary: $U$-statistics play a central role in statistical inference. In many modern applications, however, acquiring the labels required for $U$-statistics is costly. Motivated by recent advances in active inference, we develop an active inference framework for $U$-statistics that selectively queries informative labels to improve estimation efficiency under a fixed labeling budget, while preserving valid statistical inference. Our approach is built on the augmented inverse probability weighting $U$-statistic, which is designed to incorporate the sampling rule and machine learning predictions. We characterize the optimal sampling rule that minimizes its variance and design practical sampling strategies. We further extend the framework to $U$-statistic-based empirical risk minimization. Experiments on real datasets demonstrate substantial gains in estimation efficiency over baseline methods, while maintaining target coverage.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an active inference framework for U-statistics, focusing on efficient label acquisition in scenarios where labeling is costly. It uses an augmented inverse probability weighting U-statistic to incorporate sampling rules and machine learning predictions to minimize variance under a limited labeling budget. The authors aim to optimize sampling strategies and perform U-statistic-based empirical risk minimization.
data_sources: Mentioned usage of 'real datasets', which need further investigation to determine if applicable to financial domain data e.g. order book data, market sentiment scores, etc. Otherwise applicability is reduced.
alpha_potential: The potential alpha lies in more efficient feature/signal discovery. U-statistics can be used to test for patterns or relationships in financial data but computationally expensive. This approach can reduce the data requirements to achieve a set confidence interval in detecting the pattern. It allows for faster backtesting and more efficient identification of potentially profitable relationships.

title: VNDUQE: Information-Theoretic Novelty Detection using Deep Variational Information Bottleneck
summary: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples is critical for safe deployment of neural networks in safety-critical applications. While maximum softmax probability (MSP) provides a simple baseline, it lacks theoretical grounding and suffers from miscalibration. We propose VNDUQE (VIB-based Novelty Detection and Uncertainty Quantification for Nondestructive Evaluation), which investigates novelty detection through the Deep Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB), which explicitly constrains information flow through learned representations. We train VIB models on MNIST with held-out digit classes and evaluate OOD detection using information-theoretic metrics: KL divergence and prediction entropy. Our results reveal complementary detection signals: KL divergence achieves perfect detection (100\% AUROC on noise) on far-OOD samples (noise, domain shift), while prediction entropy excels at near-OOD detection (94.7\% AUROC on novel digit classes). A parallel detection strategy combining both metrics achieves 95.3\% average AUROC and 92\% true positive rate at 5\% false positive rate, which is a 32 percentage point improvement over baseline MSP (85.0\% AUROC, 60.1\% TPR). Compression via the information bottleneck principle ($β=10^{-3}$) reduces Expected Calibration Error by 38\%, demonstrating that information-theoretic constraints produce fundamentally more reliable uncertainty estimates. These findings directly support active learning with expensive computational oracles, where well-calibrated novelty detection enables principled threshold selection for oracle queries.
core_methodology: The paper proposes VNDUQE, a novelty detection method utilizing a Deep Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB). It aims to identify out-of-distribution (OOD) samples by explicitly constraining information flow through learned representations. Detection is performed using KL divergence and prediction entropy, combined in a parallel strategy. VIB aims to improve calibration and uncertainty quantification.
data_sources: The paper uses MNIST for demonstration, which is a dataset of handwritten digits. This is NOT a financial data source. However, the *method* could conceivably be applied to financial time series or alternative data where OOD detection is important.
alpha_potential: The alpha potential lies in identifying regime shifts, anomalies, or unusual market behavior. By detecting 'out-of-distribution' events, a trader might be able to avoid tail risk, adapt to new market dynamics faster, or identify rare arbitrage opportunities, assuming the method can be adapted to financial data.
